poster_title: MLP Memory: A Retriever-Pretrained Memory for Large Language Models
authors: Rubin Wei, Jiaqi Cao, Jiarui Wang, Jushi Kai, Qipeng Guo, Bowen Zhou, Zhouhan Lin
paper_info: LUMIA Lab, School of Artificial Intelligence, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai AI Laboratory; Department of Electronic Engineering, Tsinghua University; SJTU Paris Elite Institute of Technology; 2023

panels.headline: Decoder-only LLMs excel in tasks but struggle with effective knowledge utilization.
content: Decoder-only LLMs are powerful but have limitations in knowledge utilization.
Non-parametric RAG methods offer flexible knowledge access but introduce high latency.
Parametric fine-tuning methods are efficient but risk catastrophic forgetting.
There is a need for a method that combines the benefits of both approaches.

panels.headline: The trade-off between efficient inference and effective knowledge access is a significant challenge.
content: LLMs require a balance between inference efficiency and knowledge access.
Current methods either introduce high latency or degrade general performance.
A scalable and generalizable solution is needed to enhance knowledge utilization.
The method should be adaptable to different model architectures and datasets.

panels.headline: MLP Memory learns to internalize retrieval patterns during training.
content: Propose MLP Memory, a lightweight parametric module.
Pretrain the MLP to imitate a k-NN retriever's behavior.
Integrate the pretrained MLP Memory with Transformer decoders.
panels.figure_caption: Approaches to enhance factual accuracy and knowledge utilization. Top left: Nonparametric RAG provides flexible knowledge access but suffers from high latency. Top right: Parametric fine-tuning risks catastrophic forgetting. Bottom: MLP Memory learns retrieval patterns during training.

panels.headline: 17.5% scaling gains on WikiText-103 and 24.1% on Web datasets.
content: Evaluate on WikiText-103 and Web datasets.
Test on five QA benchmarks and nine general NLP tasks.
Measure inference efficiency (time to first token and tokens per second).
12.3% relative improvement on five QA benchmarks.
5.2 points absolute gain on nine general NLP tasks.
2.5 × faster inference than RAG and 5.6 × faster than kNN-LM.
panels.figure_caption: Performance and efficiency comparison. Left: accuracy across three QA benchmarks. MLP Memory consistently outperforms the base model, surpassing both parametric methods (CPT, LoRA) and non-parametric retrieval (RAG). Right: inference efficiency, measured by time to first token (TTFT, ↓).

panels.headline: MLP Memory provides comprehensive and accurate responses.
content: MLP Memory reduces hallucinations by up to 10 points on HaluEval.
The method's effectiveness may vary with different model architectures and datasets.
panels.figure_caption: RAG system distracted by retrieved content fails to answer the question, while MLP Memory provides comprehensive and accurate response.

panels.headline: MLP Memory offers a lightweight and efficient solution for enhancing knowledge utilization in LLMs.
content: MLP Memory bridges the gap between efficient inference and effective knowledge access.
It achieves significant performance gains and faster inference compared to existing methods.
MLP Memory provides a practical alternative to RAG and fine-tuning approaches.
The method is scalable and generalizable, suitable for various LLMs and datasets.
Future work can explore the method's application to different model architectures and tasks.
